outputs.exact_statement: If $\mathsf{ZF}$ is consistent, then so is $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{PP}+\mathsf{AC}_{\mathrm{WO}}+\neg\mathsf{AC}$.

Let $V$ be a countable transitive model of $\mathsf{ZFC}$. There are a set forcing $\mathbb Q\in V$, a $V$-generic filter $G$, and a transitive symmetric submodel $W$ of $V[G]$ such that $$V\subseteq W\subseteq V[G],\qquad
 \mathrm{Ord}^W=\mathrm{Ord}^V,\qquad
 W\models\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{PP}+\mathsf{AC}_{\mathrm{WO}}+\neg\mathsf{AC}.$$ Every countable sequence of elements of $V$ that belongs to $W$ already belongs to $V$.

If a monoid has conditional joins and satisfies Equation [eq:mono-margin], every ideal in $\downarrow a$ has a nondecreasing cofinal sequence of length $\omega$, with repetitions allowed. The same conclusion holds in any $\mathsf{ZFC}$ extension in which the monoid, order, heights and costs retain their meanings, for ideals belonging to that extension.

There is a monoid $T$ of cardinality $\mu$, with a distinguished $e\ne1$, having the following properties.* 1. *$T$ is left cancellative and conical, has conditional joins, and has heights and costs satisfying Equation [eq:mono-margin].* 2. *Every valid finite overlap prescription on copies of $T$ is realized by left translations $x\mapsto l_i x$ in $T$, with exactly the prescribed identifications.* 3. *For $a,b\in T$ with $b\ne1$, and every ideal $U\subseteq\downarrow a$, there are $\mu$ distinct elements $m$ with $$\label{eq:mono-probes} \begin{gathered} mb=ae,\qquad m\not\sqsubseteq a,\qquad \downarrow m\cap\downarrow a=U,\\ n\vee m=ae\quad(n\sqsubseteq a,\ n\notin U). \end{gathered}$$ The cones of distinct elements in this family intersect exactly in $aeT$. Moreover $|T\setminus eT|=\mu$.* 4. *For every countable subset of $T$ there is a countable submonoid $T_0$ containing it and a continuous conservative tower starting at $T_0$ and ending at $T$. Each successor step has one of the following properties:* 1. *no new element divides an old element;* 2. *every new element $w$ with an old right multiple has a least old right multiple $g(w)$, and $$\label{eq:mono-gate-old} d\text{ old},\quad g(w)\sqsubseteq wd \quad\Longrightarrow\quad wd\text{ old}.$$* *Here “old” means belonging to the base of that particular successor step, and the comparisons may be tested in the final monoid.

The presented extension $M'$ is left cancellative and conical, has conditional joins, and conservatively contains $M$. Every new element with an old right multiple has a least old right multiple, and Equation [eq:mono-gate-old] holds at this extension. For $m=p_0$, $$\label{eq:mono-probe-profile} \begin{gathered} mb=ae,\qquad m\not\sqsubseteq a,\qquad \downarrow m\cap\downarrow a=\bigcup_i\downarrow n_i,\\ x\vee m=ae\qquad (x\sqsubseteq a,\ x\not\sqsubseteq m), \end{gathered}$$ where the downsets and joins in this display are computed in $M'$.
The height and cost functions on $M$ extend to the probe extension $M'$ so that Equation [eq:mono-margin] holds. For any old comparison, its missed-cost supremum is unchanged.

Let $M$ satisfy the algebraic and margin hypotheses, and let a finite nonempty overlap prescription on copies of $M$ be valid. There is a conservative extension realizing it by left translations. The extension is left cancellative and conical, has conditional joins, and admits extending heights and costs satisfying Equation [eq:mono-margin]. No new element divides an old one.

Suppose $B\subseteq M$ is conservative and both monoids have the algebraic properties above. Either extension operation with parameters in $B$ is valid over $M$, and the extension of $B$ conservatively embeds into the corresponding extension of $M$ by the same generators. A finite overlap prescription with parameters in $B$ is valid in $B$ if and only if it is valid in $M$.

Suppose a probe satisfies Equation [eq:mono-probe-profile] in one stage of a tower of the two operations. It continues to satisfy that equation at every later stage and at the union, with the full later downward closure of its original path. Previously constructed joins between probes are also preserved.

Let $(n_i)$ be a nondecreasing sequence in $T$, and choose a countable-base tower from Theorem 4 whose initial submonoid contains all $n_i$ and all right quotients between them. Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\omega\times T$ be a set of pairs such that each $(l,m)\in\mathcal A$ has $m\sqsubseteq n_N$ for some $N$. Assume that for each $(l,m)\in\mathcal A$ and each $N$ there is $(l',md)\in\mathcal A$ with $l'\geq l$, $n_ld=n_{l'}$, and $n_N\sqsubseteq md$. Then, starting from any pair in $\mathcal A$, a finite succession of these replacements reaches a pair whose second coordinate belongs to the initial countable submonoid.

The forcing $\mathbb R$ is countably closed and satisfies the $\mu$-chain condition. It adds no countable sequences of ground elements, preserves $\kappa=\aleph_1^V$, and preserves every ground cardinal at least $\mu$. In particular it preserves $\mu$ and $\mu^+$. If $V\models\mathsf{CH}$, it preserves all cardinals.

1.  *For every $p\in\mathbb P$ and ground $J\subseteq I$ of size at most $\mu$, there is $r\in\mathbb P$ with $r_e=p$ and $J\subseteq D_r$.*

2.  *A finite family $s_i\in\mathbb P$ has a common extension whenever each pair has either disjoint ranges or an intersection that is exactly the range of a common subdiagram $$s_{i,a_{ij}}=s_{j,a_{ji}}.$$*

3.  *A partial placement of finitely many diagrams that is injective and consistent on their specified common parts, extends to a ground permutation of $I$. Unspecified coordinates of these diagrams and of finitely many Cohen conditions can be placed outside any prescribed ground set of size at most $\mu$.

The symmetric forcing relation is definable formula by formula in $V$, and it forces every axiom instance of full pure-set $\mathsf{ZF}$. If $V$ is externally transitive, the evaluated class $W$ is a transitive model of that theory, with $$V\subseteq W\subseteq V[F][H], \qquad \mathrm{Ord}^W=\mathrm{Ord}^{V[F][H]}.$$ The truth lemma holds for this evaluated model. Over an arbitrary countable choice ground, it holds for the symmetric quotient of internal names described in Section 8.

Fix an $\mathbb R$-generic $F$.*

1.  *If $p\in\mathbb P$ and all product-name parameters $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k$ are supported by $D_p$, then $p$ decides each ordinary $\mathbb P$-forcing formula $\varphi(\tau_1[F],\ldots,\tau_k[F])$ in $V[F]$. The parameters may have arbitrary rank.*

2.  *Suppose a Cohen condition $d$ forces that $s\Vdash_{\mathbb P}\varphi(\vec\tau[F])$, where all the product names are supported by $D_s$. Then $d\restriction(D_s\times\kappa)$ forces the same assertion.*

*For brevity we write $d\restriction D_s$ for this restriction.

Suppose $s_0,s_1\leq p$ and $D_{s_0}\cap D_{s_1}=D_p$. Let $\sigma_i$ be product $\mathrm{HS}$ names supported by $D_{s_i}$. Fix an $\mathbb R$-generic $F$. If some $v\leq s_0,s_1$ forces $\sigma_0[F]=\sigma_1[F]$ in ordinary $\mathbb P$-forcing, then there is a product $\mathrm{HS}$ name $\sigma$, supported by $D_p$, such that $$s_i\Vdash_{\mathbb P}\sigma[F]=\sigma_i[F]
 \qquad(i=0,1)$$ in $V[F]$. The names may have arbitrary rank. If, in $V[F]$, each $s_i$ also forces $\sigma_i[F]\subseteq A$, the descended name can be normalized to a subset name with only label names as possible members.
In $W$, every nonempty set $X$ is the image of a surjection $A\times\eta\to X$ for some ordinal $\eta$. No bound on the rank of $X$ is imposed.
The model $W$ satisfies $\mathsf{AC}_{\mathrm{WO}}$: every ordinal-indexed family of nonempty sets in $W$ has a choice function in $W$.
The set $A$ is not wellorderable in $W$. In particular $W\models\neg\mathsf{AC}$.
For every ground set $X$, every function $f:\omega\to X$ belonging to $W$ belongs to $V$. Consequently $W$ adds no countable sequences of ground elements.
For every $F$ as above and every ground $r\le q$, $|\mathcal D_F(r)|\le\mu$ in $V[F]$.
Each set in Equations [eq:class-availability] and [eq:label-availability] is an ideal of $\downarrow a$. Every ideal of $\downarrow a$ in $V[F]$ belongs to $V$.

For every $r\le q$ and every nonempty ideal $U\subseteq\downarrow a$, where $q=r_a$, both $B_{r,U}(F)$ and $L_{r,U}$ have cardinality $\mu$ in $V[F]$. The label fiber already has that cardinality in $V$.

For every contraction $v\to w$, the label fibers satisfy $L_v=L_w$, and inclusion of symbolic elements gives a bijection $B_w(F)\longrightarrow B_v(F)$. These identifications commute with composition.
In the ground model, $|G_C/K_C|\le\aleph_0$.
For every $k\in K_C$, transport $T_k^F$ is an order isomorphism from $(B_C(F),<_F)$ to $(B_C(kF),<_{kF})$. The group $K_C$ fixes $L_C$ pointwise.

Formula [eq:detector-pattern] is independent of the representative of $\pi K_C$. For each $F$ there is an $\alpha<\kappa$ at which all distinct cosets have distinct patterns. There is a definable selection $c_C(F)\in\Gamma_C$ satisfying $$\label{eq:coset-selector-covariance} c_C(\sigma F)=\sigma c_C(F)\qquad(\sigma\in G_C).$$
In $W$, every nonwellorderable surjective image of $A$ is in bijection with $A$.

Work in $\mathsf{ZF}$. Suppose that a nonempty set $A$ has the following properties.*

1.  *For every nonempty set $X$, there are an ordinal $\eta$ and a surjection $A\times\eta\longrightarrow X$.*

2.  *Every ordinal-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function.*

3.  *Every nonwellorderable surjective image of $A$ is in bijection with $A$.*

*Then $\mathsf{PP}$ holds: for all sets $X,Y$, every surjection $f:X\longrightarrow Y$ has an injection $j:Y\longrightarrow X$.
In $\mathsf{ZF}$, if a set $A$ is not wellorderable, then $\mathcal P(A)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ has no choice function.

Let $V$ be a ground model of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, put $$\kappa=\omega_1^V,\qquad \mu=\bigl((2^{\aleph_0})^+\bigr)^V, \qquad |I|^V=\mu^+,$$ and use the monoid of Theorem 4 and the symmetric system constructed above. In an ordinary generic extension for its product forcing, the resulting symmetric model $W$ satisfies $$W\models\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{PP}+\mathsf{AC}_{\mathrm{WO}}+\neg\mathsf{AC}.$$ It contains $V$ and has the same ordinals as $V$. It adds no countable sequences of ground elements: if $b\in V$ and $z\in W$ is a function $\omega\longrightarrow b$, then $z\in V$. The set of labels $A$ is not wellorderable in $W$, and $$\mathcal P^W(A)\setminus\{\varnothing\}$$ is an explicit family in $W$ with no choice function in $W$.

For every axiom $\alpha$ of $\mathsf{ZFC}+V=L$, its relativization $\alpha^L$ is provable in $\mathsf{ZF}$. Consequently $$\operatorname{Con}(\mathsf{ZF})\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC}+V=L).$$ Moreover, $\mathsf{ZFC}+V=L$ proves the generalized continuum hypothesis.

For each standard first-order formula $\varphi$ and internal hereditarily symmetric names $\vec\tau$, $$W\models\varphi([\vec\tau]_G)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (\exists p\in G)\ M\models
      p\Vdash_{\mathrm{HS}_{\mathcal S}}\varphi(\vec\tau).$$ In particular $W\models\mathsf{ZF}$.
